questions.q: Why are IAM roles generally preferred over IAM users for services like EC2 instances?
options: Roles are easier to name than users
Roles use temporary, auto-expiring credentials instead of long-term access keys that can leak
Roles can only be used by humans, not services
Roles automatically grant administrator access
questions.explain: A role is assumed for temporary credentials rather than holding long-lived access keys, removing the risk of keys leaking into a repository or log file.

questions.q: What does a role's trust policy define?
options: What AWS actions the role can perform
Which principal is allowed to assume the role
The expiration date of the role itself
The billing account the role is charged to
questions.explain: The trust policy (assume-role policy) defines who can assume the role. It grants no AWS permissions on its own — that's the permissions policy's job.

questions.q: In the example policy scoped to "arn:aws:s3:::nb-checkout-logs/*" with action "s3:GetObject", what does this demonstrate?
options: A policy with no practical restrictions
A least-privilege permissions policy limited to read access on one specific bucket
A trust policy defining who can assume the role
A policy that grants full S3 access across the account
questions.explain: The policy grants only GetObject (read) on one bucket's ARN, in contrast to a wildcard policy using s3:* and Resource: * that would grant far broader access.

questions.q: Why does a tight permissions policy alone not guarantee a secure role?
options: Permissions policies are ignored by AWS
The trust policy also matters — if the wrong principal can assume the role, the permissions still apply to that unintended assumer
Permissions policies cannot be scoped to specific resources
AWS does not support permissions policies on roles
questions.explain: A role is only as secure as both policies together — a narrow permissions policy doesn't help if an overly broad trust policy lets an unintended principal assume the role.

questions.q: What is an ARN used for in an IAM policy?
options: Authenticating a user's password
Uniquely identifying the specific AWS resource a policy statement applies to
Encrypting data at rest
Defining the trust relationship between accounts
questions.explain: An ARN (Amazon Resource Name) scopes a policy statement to one specific resource, such as one S3 bucket, rather than every resource of that type.
